utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is IT-04-84-R77.2, the Prosecutor versus Avni Krasniqi. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Due to my absence when preparing this Initial Appearance, Judge Hoepfel took the lead in preparing and will take the lead during this hearing. Judge Hoepfel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. May I first have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, David Re, assisted by Christopher Gosnell and case manager, Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Your Honours, Michiel Pestman for the Defence, all on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Krasniqi --

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: And my client, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And may I ask the accused to give us the complete name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 18th of the 5th, 1969.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And your name once more?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Avni Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please have a seat. Now, Mr. Krasniqi, this is your appearance here, so-called Initial Appearance, after your arrest and surrender to the United Nations Detention Unit. This exercise is aimed at the judicial supervision of your arrest, of your position. And to make it absolutely clear to you, I would like to point out that we are here sitting in a case which is separate from the case against Haradinaj, Balaj, and Brahimaj. This is a pure contempt case and therefore the Defence in that other case is not present. Now, as your to your own case and situation, did the counsel explain to you the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And have you also received the indictment in your own language? Could you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. And did you or do you understand it after also having talked with the counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only had a few minutes to consult. Not very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. Do you want to have the indictment read out loudly? Would that be necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's up to you, actually. If you have read it, you also have the possibility to waive your right. And if you want to consult with counsel for a moment, please do so. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Pestman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes, we haven't been able to discuss this particular issue yet. I can discuss it in two minutes with my client, but there is no interpreter present. So if -- I can do it in court. I don't have to go anywhere. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: With the help of an interpreter, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Could an interpreter come and help for this private conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I can help out. An interpreter is on the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe in the meantime, I might mention -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The indictment. Please, as you don't understand it -- Is there an Albanian interpreter present? Thank you. And here -- please, you can go on now with your private conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Pestman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PESTMAN
utterances.text: Yes. He would like to have it read out to him. Although he has received a copy in Albanian, he would like to have it read out as well so that he completely understands the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. I can do it myself. We have a corrected version of this indictment received today. It was only a small technical mistake which has been corrected. The original indictment was filed on 5th of November, and I will read now the indictment. The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, case number -- I don't have to repeat it, I think. The Prosecutor against Avni Krasniqi, Indictment. The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia and Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, charges: Avni Krasniqi, with contempt of the Tribunal. The accused, Avni Krasniqi, was born on 18th of May, 1969 in Vranoc in the municipality of Pec in Kosovo. Charges. Contempt of the Tribunal. 1. On 29th of October, 2007, Avni Krasniqi committed - that is the charge - committed contempt of the Tribunal by knowingly and wilfully interfering with the administration of justice by failing to comply with an order to appear before the Trial Chamber in the case of Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj, Case No. IT-04-84- this was the correction - T, without just excuse. 2. On 19th of October, 2007, the Trial Chamber issued a subpoena ad testificandum against Avni Krasniqi and ordered him to appear to testify before the Tribunal on 29 October 2007. 3. On 23 October 2007, a Prosecution investigator, Ljobomir Jozefciak informed Avni Krasniqi by telephone that the subpoena had been issued against him. On 24 October 2007, Mr. Jozefciak went to Avni Krasniqi's home and gave him a copy of the subpoena. Avni Krasniqi refused to sign the receipt of the subpoena but gave Mr. Jozefciak a handwritten explanation for his unwillingness to testify. Mr. Jozefciak explained to the witness the availability of protective measures which can alleviate Avni Krasniqi's concerns. Avni Krasniqi insisted that he was not willing to testify. 4. On 25th of October, 2007, UNMIK officer Cardil Kadralj [phoen] served the subpoena on Avni Krasniqi, who received it but refused to sign the memorandum of service and repeated that he was not willing to testify. 5. On 29th of October, 2007, Avni Krasniqi failed to appear before the Trial Chamber without just excuse. By these acts and omissions, Avni Krasniqi committed Contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent powers under Rule 77(A)(iii) of the Rules of the Tribunal. Carla Del Ponte, Prosecutor, The Hague, Netherlands. Now, as I would like to discuss health issues, among others, I would like to go into private session. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please. For the rest of this contempt case, I would deem it appropriate to adjourn right now sine die. What does the Presiding Judge, mean? May I hand -- may I hand over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think in closed session we discussed health issues. The Chamber did not want to enter into any discussion on the merits of the case, which clearly is part of the defence and not something to be dealt with in private session. So the reasons why Mr. Krasniqi thinks that he had -- that he was right in refusing to testify already gives a bit of an indication on -- on whether he pleads guilty or not guilty. But since you also indicated that a plea would be entered not today and since under the Rules Mr. Krasniqi has 30 days to enter a plea, at this moment the Chamber will not push any -- push Mr. Krasniqi to enter a plea and, rather, give him an opportunity to think about it and to enter a plea when we have resumed. It should be clear that this contempt case is separate from the other case in which Mr. Krasniqi was called as a witness. Whether and to what extent the testimony, if Mr. Krasniqi would decide that he would testify, will have any influence on this case, is not for the Chamber, certainly not at this moment, to decide. If there are ever any reasons to withdraw the indictment -- the indictment has been confirmed. So that means that the Prosecutor should file a motion to withdraw the indictment. If there are any reasons to do so, the Chamber is not part of that. Therefore, as far as this contempt case is concerned -- as far as this contempt case is concerned, we should adjourn. At the same time, I would like to refer to Rule 57, which deals with the procedure after arrest as far as detention is concerned. Detention and remand follows under the Rules once an accused has been arrested. Therefore, to the extent necessary, it is ordered hereby, although it follows already from the Rules, but to follow the tradition of this Tribunal, a written confirmation of the detention or remand will follow. And I take it, Mr. Pestman, that since you have not had much time until now to discuss matters with Mr. Krasniqi, that there will be an opportunity soon for you to go more thoroughly through the present situation with your client. Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment? Not Prosecution. Not Defence. Then we adjourn sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.01 p.m.,
